interviewscam.com is run by {{< param operator >}}. You can find Replikanti on [GitHub](https://github.com/Replikanti). The site collects the names that fake job interviews use, so you can check one in the minutes before a call.

## Why this site exists

In early November 2026 I was invited to an interview with a web3 company. The meeting link arrived 15 minutes before the call. It pointed to a meeting platform I had never heard of, and it only worked on Windows and macOS. A web search for the company name returned nothing relevant.

This is a common pattern. Fake interviews have become a standard way to infect developers with info-stealers. Security vendors publish thorough reports. They come later, they are written for security teams, and they use the names of malware families. A candidate sees a company, an app or a domain, and has only minutes to decide. Campaigns also rename their apps and companies faster than new reports appear.

This site keeps one page per name a candidate sees. Where a cited source links the name to a campaign family, the page names that family and the source. Otherwise the page says the name is unattributed.

## How it works

Reports arrive by email and are reviewed before anything is published. Pages describe artifacts such as domains, app names and file hashes, not verdicts about companies. The [methodology](/methodology/) has the details.
